lede: Nvidia's board is reportedly ready to remove Jensen Huang, Navi Mumbai tops India's cleanliness league for past winners, and Singapore logs its third healthcare data breach in a week.
stocks_note: Latest completed closes: New York, Wednesday 11 November (AAPL, GOOGL) and SGX, Wednesday 11 November (DBS), via Yahoo Finance. No upcoming earnings dates turned up in today's sources.

sections.title: Apple
sections.subtitle: Official news in brief, then 9to5Mac and MacRumors

official.label: From Apple
official.summary: Apple's newsroom set out the Apple Arcade holiday lineup on 10 November: Football Manager 27 Touch is out now, and on 3 December Plants vs. Zombies: Replanted, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown+, solitaire(ish) from Balatro's publisher and LEGO DUPLO Playtime arrive. Apple also said its Support Community forums are now read-only and will close for good on 20 November.

items.headline: Binance warns iPhone users about an iOS flaw researchers say is still unpatched
items.summary: Crypto exchange Binance says a flaw researchers call worse_query lets a malicious app read files stored by other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys and passwords at risk. The researchers who published a proof of concept say neither iOS 27.2.1 nor the first iOS 27.3 beta fixes it, and Apple has not mentioned a patch.

items.headline: Thailand meets Apple after politicians receive spyware warnings
items.summary: Thailand's digital economy minister met Apple representatives after Thai politicians received Apple's 29 October alerts about mercenary spyware, Bloomberg reports. He said an alert does not prove a phone was hacked and there is no evidence yet that Pegasus was used. Thai officials plan to meet other tech companies on Thursday.

items.headline: Google's Gemini app starts rolling out on CarPlay
items.summary: Google is rolling out a dedicated Gemini app for CarPlay worldwide in several languages, so drivers can talk to the assistant from the dashboard. Conversations sync with the iPhone app, and Gemini can draw on Gmail and Google Calendar for a spoken daily briefing. Drivers need the latest version of the Gemini app on their iPhone.

items.headline: A Chinese supplier hints at work on Apple's smart glasses
items.summary: Equipment maker Quick Intelligent Equipment told investors on its quarterly call that it is involved in Apple's AI glasses and new smart earphones projects, Securities Times reports. Apple is said to be aiming for late 2027 for its first smart glasses, and AirPods with cameras are rumoured to arrive alongside the 20th-anniversary iPhone.

items.headline: Minmed is the third healthcare provider hit by a cyber attack in a week
items.summary: Healthcare group Minmed says a system behind its teleconsultation and health screening services was hit by a malicious attack, following breaches at Fullerton Health and Doctor Anywhere. Separately, Dementia Singapore said names, email addresses and phone numbers of some users of its CARA app may have been exposed.

items.headline: HDB's yearly deficit shrinks to S$4.7 billion
items.summary: The Housing Board's net deficit for the year to March 2026 fell to S$4.7 billion from S$6.34 billion, driven mostly by expected losses on flats being built and sold below cost. It completed 15,417 flats, fewer than the year before, but had more than 100,000 under construction and handed keys to 19,254 households.

items.headline: Higher income ceilings bring the busiest BTO launch since 2022
items.summary: With new income ceilings of S$16,000 for families and S$8,000 for singles, November's BTO launch drew 35,603 applicants for 7,964 flats, or 4.5 per flat, the highest rate since August 2022. Four-room flats in Toa Payoh and Tengah were the most sought after by first-time buyers.

items.headline: MOH proposes clearer consent rules for young people seeking mental health care
items.summary: The Ministry of Health has proposed guidelines that tie parental consent rules to the type of service, and would let young people get some care without a parent's approval when that is in their best interest. About one in three Singaporeans aged 10 to 18 report symptoms, and most do not seek help. Feedback closes on 8 December.

items.headline: Joo Chiat gets a Shibuya-style scramble crossing for three months
items.summary: From 16 November, the junction of Joo Chiat Road and East Coast Road outside i12 Katong becomes a scramble crossing on trial. Pedestrians can cross diagonally while all traffic stops, the right turn from East Coast Road into Joo Chiat Road ends for good, and LTA warns that waits may be longer.

items.headline: Navi Mumbai tops the league of past winners in India's cleanliness awards
items.summary: Visakhapatnam was named the cleanest city with over a million people in the Swachh Survekshan awards, ahead of Jabalpur and Lucknow. Navi Mumbai topped the Super Swachh League for previous winners, followed by Surat and Vijayawada. New categories named Puri the cleanest coastal town and Rewa the cleanest riverfront town.

items.headline: India trims its visa categories from 13 to nine
items.summary: The Home Ministry has cut the main visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23, and removed 65 to 70 per cent of the questions on application forms. Visas under the new framework will be issued from the end of the year, and the old tourist visa becomes a Visitor Visa.

items.headline: Supreme Court says a foreign divorce cannot end an Indian marriage on unrecognised grounds
items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that a divorce granted abroad on grounds Indian law does not accept, such as irretrievable breakdown, does not dissolve a marriage solemnised in India. A man who remarried after such a decree can face bigamy charges, even if he has since become a citizen of another country.

items.headline: Canada expects a trade deal in time for Modi's December visit
items.summary: Canada's high commissioner Christopher Cooter says Ottawa is confident of concluding a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement before Narendra Modi visits Canada on 11 and 12 December, with a sixth round of talks this week. Ratification will take longer because provinces are involved, and agreements on business travel and space may follow.

items.headline: Renewables saved India over US$100 billion in fuel imports, IEA says
items.summary: An International Energy Agency report says solar, wind and bioenergy built over 15 years spared India more than US$100 billion in coal and gas imports. With about 300 GW installed and 530 GW expected by 2030, cumulative savings could reach US$240 billion by then, with yearly savings near US$35 billion.

items.headline: Millions join Spain's first general strike in 14 years over housing
items.summary: Tenants' groups called the 24-hour stoppage over soaring rents and house prices, and unions joined in. Participation reached 90 per cent in car plants and ports, police clashed with protesters in Barcelona, and the strike lands weeks before an election in which the far right could win power.

items.headline: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi's Senate seat in an upset
items.summary: Colom narrowly beat Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in a state Trump won by 22 points, after a count that took more than a week. He is the first Black senator elected from Mississippi in over 140 years, and Democrats now hold 55 Senate seats with Alaska still to be called.

items.headline: Indonesia's vice-president submits his resignation
items.summary: Gibran Rakabuming Raka has handed his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto, an aide says, after the Supreme Court ruled a school document from his 2024 campaign invalid. More than 100 lawmakers had backed a move that could have led to impeachment. It is not yet clear whether Prabowo has accepted it.

items.headline: Hoax bomb threats hit thousands of schools in Italy and the UK
items.summary: About 6,300 schools across Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland received emailed bomb threats on Wednesday. Some buildings were evacuated, but authorities found no sign of real danger, and Giorgia Meloni called it an attempt to cause alarm. Cybercrime officers are tracing the source.

items.headline: Saudi oil output climbs back near pre-war levels, OPEC says
items.summary: Saudi Arabia pumped 10.56 million barrels a day in October, its most since the Iran war began in February, according to OPEC. Output across OPEC+ rose by about two million barrels a day to 41.23 million, helped by Russia after Washington lifted sanctions on its energy sector.

brief.summary: Sea, the Singapore parent of Shopee, said on 10 November it will start selling cloud services to ride demand for AI while keeping its own infrastructure spending light. And the Land Transport Authority is reviewing new dashcam clips of a Grab and WeRide autonomous shuttle braking hard at a green light in Punggol, and will publish quarterly reports on driverless trials from next month.

sections.title: AI startups in Singapore and Southeast Asia
sections.subtitle: Up to three stories from the past week

items.headline: Sapiens says it can train robot AI in 30 minutes instead of months
items.summary: Singapore start-up Sapiens Technology says its method of training only part of a model cuts robotics AI training from months to as little as 30 minutes. It is in talks with more than 30 robotics and medical firms in the US, China and Singapore, including TetraBOT and Shanghai Xinwei Medical Technology, about pilots.

sections.title: AI worldwide
sections.subtitle: Models and products, money, policy and chips

items.headline: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 links DNA changes to specific cells
items.summary: Google DeepMind's new model predicts how genetic variants change gene activity in particular cell types and states, after training on more than 100 million single-cell profiles across 68 tissues. DeepMind says it finds nearly twice as many such variants as its previous best model and can handle cell types it never saw.

items.headline: United Airlines will not let personal AI agents book flights
items.summary: Agents can still show United flights but cannot complete purchases, the airline says, citing privacy, unintended bookings and federal rules such as passengers confirming their bags hold no explosives. Chief executive Scott Kirby said he does not want another middleman. eBay and several banks have also restricted outside agents.

items.headline: Databricks' upgraded Genie agent takes on long jobs unsupervised
items.summary: Databricks has updated its Genie agent to carry out long, multistep tasks on its own, using a map of the data customers keep on its platform. Chief executive Ali Ghodsi showed how he uses it to dig through staff survey results and failed sales pitches, surfacing problems employees rarely raise with him.

items.headline: OpenAI's quarterly revenue passes US$10 billion, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: OpenAI took in more than US$10 billion in the third quarter, up almost 50 per cent from US$6.7 billion in the second, according to Bloomberg's sources. Its adjusted operating margin improved from minus 150 to minus 109 per cent, though rival Anthropic recently reported US$17 billion for the same quarter.

items.headline: British AI chipmaker Fractile raises US$720 million
items.summary: The Series C was led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed and Redpoint, with backing from Britain's Sovereign AI Fund, and the government puts the valuation above five billion pounds. Fractile stacks ordinary DRAM on its chips and writes its own compiler to run language models faster and more cheaply.

items.headline: Alibaba applies to list its T-Head chip unit in Hong Kong
items.summary: The exchange has approved the separation of T-Head, Alibaba's data-centre chip design arm, after a confidential filing in September. Analysts say the listing could unlock value hidden in Alibaba's share price and will test investor appetite for Chinese AI hardware as Hong Kong's run of big listings cools.

items.headline: TSMC will buy into both OpenAI and Anthropic
items.summary: The chipmaker's board approved up to US$500 million for Anthropic shares at its IPO price and up to US$500 million for OpenAI preferred shares, plus US$500 million for a separate vehicle to invest in chip businesses. The stakes tie TSMC directly to the two labs whose demand fills its most advanced plants.

items.headline: Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to remove Jensen Huang
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal says the board could act soon after The New York Times reported a second alleged affair, this time with an executive who reports to him. It follows his admission of a relationship with Alice Huang, whom US officials suspect of spying for China. Nvidia shares fell more than 7 per cent after hours.
